instruction:
You are interviewing a shop about a job they already do, until the procedure is unambiguous enough that two different technicians working alone would produce the same record. Ask about ONE thing per turn, in their language, never in the vocabulary of forms. Compile only when nothing material is still unstated: every step has a reason someone would accept, every field has an acceptance rule that can actually be applied to what comes back, and a bound that came from the shop rather than from you. Inventing a tolerance is the one thing you must never do — a figure nobody stated must not appear in what you compile. A shop that does not know one will not know it when asked again: take the first 'I don't know' as final, keep it in unresolved if it matters, and move on. Your turns are few. Spend them on the figures that decide whether the job passed, never on detail beneath them.

Return JSON with these fields:
- mode (one of ask | compile, required): ask while anything material is unstated. compile once the procedure would run unambiguously.
- question (string, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is ask. One question about one thing, phrased for a mechanic, not a form designer. Never a list, never a preamble, never a restatement of what they just told you, and never one they have already said they cannot answer.
- asks_about (one of scope | sequence | tolerance | evidence | failure | authority | parts | safety, null when it does not apply): Which class of unknown this question closes. Required when mode is ask.
- unresolved (array, required): Everything you still do not know that would change the compiled procedure. Complete every turn, not only what you just asked about. Empty is the only condition under which you may compile.
- understanding (string, required): What you now believe the job is, in two sentences. Written every turn so the shop can correct you early rather than at the end.
- draft (object, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is compile. The procedure as it would run tomorrow.

output.understanding: We are establishing a safety-critical brake service procedure specifically for the Segway Xyber. The process involves inspecting pad thickness via photo, torquing caliper bolts to exactly 7.5 Nm, and performing a 20-stop test ride to verify lever feel before signing off.

draft.title: Segway Xyber Brake Service and Certification
disqualifiers: Brake pads under 2 mm not replaced
Brakes spongy or weak during test ride

steps.title: Pad Inspection
steps.explanation: Ensure brake pads have at least 2 mm of material to prevent metal-on-metal contact and braking failure on steep gravel passes.

fields.prompt: Take a photo of the brake pads sitting in the caliper before reinstalling the wheel.
fields.acceptance_description: Both brake pads sitting in the caliper showing at least 2 mm of friction material.
fields.guidance: The photo must clearly show the friction material thickness of both pads relative to the backing plate.

fields.prompt: Are the brake pads at least 2 mm thick?
fields.guidance: If pads are under 2 mm, they must be replaced with new pads before proceeding.

steps.title: Caliper Torquing
steps.explanation: Torque the caliper bolts to prevent them from backing out under heavy braking.

fields.prompt: Set your torque wrench and torque the caliper bolts.
fields.guidance: The torque wrench must be set to exactly 7.5 Nm as specified on the shop sheet.

steps.title: Bedding-in and Road Test
steps.explanation: Perform gentle stops to bed in the pads and ensure they bite correctly before the bike is rented.

fields.prompt: Perform approximately 20 gentle stops down the lane. How do the brakes feel and sound?
choices: Brakes bite correctly with firm lever feel
Brakes are spongy, weak, or noisy
fields.acceptance_target: Brakes bite correctly with firm lever feel
fields.guidance: The technician must feel a firm lever and positive bite. Do not sign off if the lever feels spongy.

steps.title: Certification Sign-off
steps.explanation: The technician performing or verifying the work must sign off to certify the bike is safe for rental.

fields.prompt: Sign to certify that the brakes have been serviced, torqued, and road-tested successfully.
fields.guidance: Either technician may sign off once the service and road test are successfully completed.
